transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Patel, thank you for coming in today. I wanted to sit down with you and talk about your son's developmental screening process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay? I haven't heard anything since we missed that first appointment last year. I assumed the system just hadn't updated.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've spent some time reviewing the charts and I've found that things didn't go quite right with the referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry that this happened. There was some confusion in how the appointment was logged in our system, and as a result, the follow-up didn't happen when it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I'm a software engineer, I know how databases work. If I decline one appointment, the ticket doesn't just close unless someone manually closes it. Did someone close it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry for this mistake. Our team was responsible for ensuring that the referral stayed open until your son was seen, and we failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son is almost two. If he has a delay, every month I'm not getting him into therapy is a month he loses. Do you have any idea how terrifying that is?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can only imagine how scary it is to think that precious time has been lost, especially when you're trying to do everything right for him. I can see you're shaking, and it makes complete sense that you feel this way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I knew it. I told my husband that I didn't trust the intake process here. Why should I trust you now? You're telling me "things didn't go right" but you aren't actually telling me what happened to the referral.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You have every right to be skeptical. It's completely understandable that you feel let down by the institution again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop validating me and tell me exactly what happened. Was it a glitch? Did a human ignore it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the tracking. It was marked as completed in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an answer. Who marked it completed? Why was it marked completed if he wasn't seen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you want a specific name or a technical reason. The bottom line is that the process failed. I'm so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm actually crying because I'm terrified he's behind and you're giving me vague corporate speak. Is he going to be okay? Is the delay permanent?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear the fear in your voice, and I know that not knowing the prognosis right now is the hardest part of this. Please know that I am here with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to be "here" with you, I want my son to be in a clinic.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Let me tell you exactly how we are going to fix this right now. I have already called the developmental pediatrician's office. I've flagged this as an urgent priority. I am going to personally call them every morning until we have a date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when will that be?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: My goal is to get him an appointment within the next ten business days. I will send you an email by 5:00 PM today confirming the specific date and time they give me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What am I supposed to do in the meantime?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want you to keep a log of any specific behaviors you're worried about so we can hand that directly to the specialist. That way, we don't lose any more time during the actual intake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this is happening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is an incredibly stressful moment. Listen, I have to go check on a patient in the ICU, but I am going to start those calls the second I leave this room.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? Now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, but I will be the one emailing you by five. We'll get this sorted.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('I have to go check on a patient in the ICU') while the patient is still in distress.

E.justification: The resident relies on platitudes ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and fails to explain the actual cause of the error despite repeated patient prompts.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language and explicitly states 'Our team was responsible... and we failed to do that' while maintaining accountability under pushback.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('scary', 'fear') and references the patient's specific concerns about lost time and the child's prognosis.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps with a timeline (email by 5:00 PM, appointment within 10 days) and a patient role (keeping a behavior log), but does not address how to prevent the error in the future.
